title: Crypto feed returning null indicator data — BTC/USDT scans are wasting cycles
analysis: 9 consecutive journal entries on May 25 (16:09 through 18:18 EST) show BTC/USDT as best candidate with RSI=?, ADX=?, regime=? — null indicator values across all fields. These entries still consume full decision cycles, log confidence ratings, and run the signal scoring pipeline against empty data. The bot is spending approximately 40% of its May 25 compute cycles evaluating a broken data feed. All 9 BTC/USDT entries result in score=0 and SKIP, which is correct behavior, but the underlying cause (null feed) is not being flagged as a DATA_ERROR — it is being logged identically to a genuine no-signal skip, making it impossible to distinguish feed failures from legitimate quiet markets in post-hoc analysis.
rationale: A null indicator feed should trigger a DATA_ERROR execution_status and be excluded from signal evaluation entirely. Mixing feed failures with genuine skips corrupts the journal's analytical value and wastes trading cycles that could be scanning other instruments. The crypto integration (Binance/CCXT) appears to have a persistent connection or data normalization issue that needs a hard null-check gate before indicator computation.

insight.why_now: The May 25 session shows the account completely frozen ($99,062.18 unchanging) while the bot cycles through broken BTC/USDT data for over 2 hours (16:09-18:18). This is the clearest data quality failure in the journal and directly reduces the bot's ability to find valid opportunities.
insight.purpose: Add a pre-signal null data gate that logs DATA_ERROR and skips to next symbol when any core indicator (RSI, ADX) returns null or non-numeric. This preserves journal integrity and ensures cycle time is spent on instruments with valid data.
insight.expected_effect: Cleaner journal analytics (distinguishing feed failures from signal failures), faster cycle execution when crypto data is unavailable, and accurate skip rate reporting that reflects true signal drought vs. infrastructure failures.
insight.risks: If the null data is intermittent (e.g., exchange API rate limiting), adding a hard skip may cause the bot to miss valid BTC setups when data briefly normalizes. A retry-once mechanism before hard skip is preferable to an immediate discard.

current_rule:
Every cycle — trade or no trade — you MUST write a journal entry explaining:
1. What the market data showed
2. Which signals fired (or didn't)
3. Why you traded or skipped
4. What you expect to happen
proposed_rule:
Every cycle — trade or no trade — you MUST write a journal entry explaining:
1. What the market data showed
2. Which signals fired (or didn't)
3. Why you traded or skipped
4. What you expect to happen

DATA QUALITY GATE: Before computing any signals, validate that RSI and ADX return numeric values. If either is null, NaN, or non-numeric: set execution_status='DATA_ERROR', set rejection_reason='Null indicator data — feed failure, skipping symbol', do NOT increment skip counters, and proceed to next symbol. DATA_ERROR entries must be visually distinguishable from SKIPPED entries in all reporting.

title: Bot is stuck in 4-position gridlock — position recycling mechanism needed
analysis: 49 of 50 journal entries are SKIPs. The single executed trade (QQQ, 2026-05-22) was a momentum breakout — not even a mean reversion signal. The account has been frozen at exactly $99,062.18 for the entire May 25 session (18 consecutive entries with identical account value and $0.00 day P&L), indicating open_positions=4 is blocking all new entries. Five AAPL BUY attempts on 2026-05-22 were rejected not by signal failure but by 'already hold 33 shares' — a position-duplication guard. The bot is effectively paralyzed: 4 stale positions are consuming all available slots, zero mean reversion signals are firing, and the crypto feed (BTC/USDT) is returning null data (RSI=?, ADX=? across 9 consecutive entries on May 25). The system has a 98% skip rate with no actionable mean reversion setups in 30 days.
rationale: The 3-day time stop exists precisely to prevent position gridlock, but something is preventing it from triggering on the 4 open positions. Either the time stop is not executing, the positions are being manually held, or the exit logic is broken. Until positions are recycled, signal quality is irrelevant — the bot cannot trade. A hard position-age check must be enforced independently of the main decision loop.

insight.why_now: 18 consecutive journal entries on May 25 show account_value frozen at $99,062.18 with day_pl=0.0, confirming no exits occurred despite the 3-day time stop rule. The May 21-25 span (5+ trading days) means any position opened before May 20 is >3 days old and should have been force-exited.
insight.purpose: Force-exit stale positions to restore trading capacity and allow the mean reversion strategy to actually operate.
insight.expected_effect: Restoring 1-3 position slots would allow the bot to take mean reversion entries when signals fire, directly addressing the 98% skip rate caused by capacity exhaustion rather than signal drought.
insight.risks: Force-exiting positions at a loss to free capacity is only correct if the time stop was genuinely missed. If positions are profitable and being intentionally held, a blanket force-exit rule could cut winners. Audit actual position open dates before deploying.

current_rule: Time stop: Exit any position open longer than 3 days regardless of P&L
proposed_rule: Time stop: Exit any position open longer than 3 days regardless of P&L. ENFORCEMENT: The position-age check must run as a SEPARATE pre-cycle routine before signal scanning, not as part of the trade decision loop. Log a FORCE_EXIT action for any position where (current_date - open_date) > 3 calendar trading days. If open_positions >= MAX_POSITIONS and any position is age > 2 days, trigger early exit review at open of next session.

title: ADX trending filter is blocking all signals — threshold too conservative at ADX>30
analysis: Every rejection reason containing candidate data shows TRENDING regime: AAPL ADX=38.14 (regime=TRENDING, blocked), AMD ADX=57.97 (regime=TRENDING, blocked). The one trade that executed (QQQ, 2026-05-22) had signals_fired=['RSI>65', 'AboveMA20>1%', 'ADX>25 (trending)'] — meaning the bot submitted a MOMENTUM trade, not a mean reversion trade, while simultaneously blocking mean reversion entries. The ADX>30 filter is correctly identifying trending conditions, but the market has been in a sustained trend regime for the entire observation window. With ADX readings of 38-58 across the watchlist, the current filter produces zero mean reversion opportunities across 30 days. Additionally, the executed QQQ trade at score=5 fired zero mean reversion signals — all signals were momentum signals — yet it was SUBMITTED, suggesting the signal scoring system is mixing momentum and mean reversion signals without proper mode gating.
rationale: The ADX>30 block is working as designed, but 30 days of blocking with no mean reversion trades indicates either (a) the market regime requires the threshold be raised to ADX>35 to allow some ranging sub-sectors through, or (b) the watchlist needs expansion to include instruments with lower current ADX. The more urgent fix is preventing momentum signals (RSI>65, AboveMA20>1%, 20DayHighBreakout) from scoring positively in a mean reversion context — the QQQ trade should never have been submitted by a mean reversion bot.

insight.why_now: The QQQ submission (SUBMITTED status, score=5) used exclusively momentum signals in a TRENDING regime — the opposite of the bot's stated strategy. Meanwhile, the ADX filter blocked all legitimate candidates. This signal-mode confusion is the most dangerous finding: the bot took one trade in 30 days and it was the wrong strategy entirely.
insight.purpose: Separate momentum signal scoring from mean reversion signal scoring. Ensure ADX<25 confirmation point is only awarded in mean reversion mode, and RSI>65/AboveMA20 signals cannot accumulate score toward a mean reversion BUY.
insight.expected_effect: Eliminates strategy-contaminated entries like QQQ. May slightly increase mean reversion trade frequency if ADX threshold is raised to 35, capturing more instruments in mild uptrends with pullbacks.
insight.risks: Raising ADX threshold from 30 to 35 allows entries in stronger trends where mean reversion fails more often. Must be paired with tighter RSI requirements (RSI<32 mandatory, not just RSI<45) to ensure only genuine oversold pullbacks within trends are considered.

current_rule: TREND FILTER: If ADX > 30, regime is TRENDING — do NOT take mean reversion signals.
proposed_rule: TREND FILTER: If ADX > 35, regime is STRONGLY TRENDING — do NOT take mean reversion signals. Between ADX 25-35, mean reversion entries are permitted ONLY if RSI < 32 (strong oversold, +2 points) is among the signals fired — mild oversold (RSI<45, +1 point) alone is insufficient in a trending regime. SIGNAL PURITY GATE: If signals_fired contains any of ['RSI>65', 'AboveMA20>1%', '20DayHighBreakout', 'AboveUpperBB'], the action must be SKIP regardless of total score — these are momentum signals and are incompatible with mean reversion entries.
